tests.contains: describe('Modal lifecycle contract (public native SDK mocks)', () => {

claims: Named completed-capture tests reject malformed/missing lengths, persistent UTF-8 byte-count mismatches, and malformed/missing child status.
Named tests preserve verified empty output, Unicode byte counts, exact recovery reads, and completed nonzero child status.
Named capture-read tests require successful native read completion and reject failed zero-byte/exact-size output or plausible metadata without replaying the child command.
Named provider-backed timeout preflight tests reject unsupported precision and malformed values before native exec, preserving supported whole-second millisecond values and omission without rounding.

Named lifecycle regressions query poll after fromId, retain successful null/zero/nonzero poll values, and propagate original lookup/termination errors without inventing a void acknowledgement payload.
scope: Historical revision-specific local regression evidence, not all-capability or current/future-tree native certification.
limitations: Only named local command and lifecycle regression cases are covered; live native behavior, other operations and full capability coverage remain unverified.
No clean dependency installation or live provider execution was performed; the existing installed dependency store was reused.
Length equality is not a checksum, arbitrary binary integrity, or remote cancellation/cleanup guarantee.
Initial launch/wait failures precede the read-cleanup scope; non-integrity errors still use existing native error text.
Installed native API declarations/implementations were inspected; mocks do not establish raw HTTP guarantees or compatibility across the entire declared SDK version range.
Timeout preflight is provider-backed only; no universal zero policy, independent daemon-route validation, hard elapsed-time bound or remote cancellation guarantee is established.
Raw poll RPC errors have no public authoritative nullable-absence discriminator; Modal remains cleanup-blocked. Poll/terminate do not prove physical deletion or billing cessation.
